topics.title: Introduction to Queue and the FIFO principle

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a queue follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle and contrast it with a stack.
Identify the FRONT (HEAD) and REAR (TAIL) ends of a queue and the operation performed at each.
Recognise real-life situations such as waiting lists and toll booths that follow a queue.
Explain why queues are used in computer science for web-server requests, OS job scheduling and print spooling.
Trace the effect of ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations on the contents of a queue.
Distinguish between the Overflow and Underflow exceptions in a queue.
Explain the role of PEEK, IS EMPTY and IS FULL in supporting enqueue and dequeue.
Implement a queue with a Python list using append() at the rear and pop(0) at the front.
Predict the output of Python queue functions such as dequeue, size and peek, including on an empty queue.

topics.title: Introduction to Deque and its operations

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a deque as a double-ended queue that can behave as a stack or a queue.
Identify situations such as browser history and undo options where a deque is useful.
Trace INSERTFRONT, INSERTREAR, DELETIONFRONT and DELETIONREAR operations on a deque.

topics.title: Implementation of Deque using Python and the palindrome check

concepts.learning_objective: Implement deque operations with Python list methods insert(0, x), append(), pop() and pop(0).
Apply the deque-based algorithm to decide whether a string is a palindrome.
